title: Vessel Farm Rising
premise: Kestrel Okafor, a rationalist property surveyor, is hired to appraise Hollowmere Farm, a house whose rooms rearrange themselves to match the memories of whoever walks through them. When a church bell that was melted down in 1911 rings across the village, Kestrel is pulled into the house's ledger of debts: in 1974, three villagers stole and buried something belonging to the dead, and the farm has been collecting interest ever since. To survive, Kestrel must uncover what was taken, return it, and decide whether justice outside the law is worth becoming part of the house's memory. In the end, Kestrel returns the stolen child's remains to her mother's grave, the bell falls silent, and Kestrel leaves — but carrying one borrowed memory of their own that was never theirs.
about_author: Edmund Zhou is the pen name of a former rural land surveyor who spent a decade cataloguing derelict properties across the English fenlands. He writes horror about buildings that remember more than the people who lived in them.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Kestrel Okafor arrives at Hollowmere Farm to appraise it for sale, measuring rooms that measure back — a hallway longer on the return trip, a window showing last winter. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dry professional skepticism curdling into unease as the house records Kestrel's own childhood bedroom in its plaster.

chapters.title: A Bell That Wasn't
chapters.summary: At dawn the village church bell rings, though parish records confirm it was melted down in 1911. Villagers react with practiced silence; an old woman tells Kestrel not to answer it. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: the first crack in disbelief — Kestrel heard their own name inside the tolling.

chapters.title: Ledger of Rooms
chapters.summary: Inside the farmhouse, Kestrel finds a surveyor's ledger from 1974 listing measurements for rooms that never existed, each annotated with names. The house begins replaying fragments: a shovel, rain, a small shoe. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: dread shifting into compulsion — someone in 1974 did this deliberately.

chapters.title: The Three Who Signed
chapters.summary: Kestrel tracks down descendants of the three signatories: a retired vicar's son, a pub landlady, and a man who never left the village. Each refuses to speak, each wears the same exhausted look. POV: rotating among the three descendants. Emotional beat: inherited guilt — they've been paying installments all their lives.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Through the house's replayed memories, Kestrel pieces together 1974: three men dug up a child's coffin from unconsecrated ground and hid her beneath the farm's foundations to stop her mother's haunting petition for a proper burial. POV: the house itself, fragmentary. Emotional beat: horror without a monster — ordinary men committing an ordinary cruelty.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: The village begins losing memories wholesale — names vanishing from gravestones, faces blurring in photographs — as the house calls in its debt. The landlady's son forgets she exists. POV: Kestrel and the vicar's son. Emotional beat: grief at erasure; time is running out because forgetting is the payment.

chapters.title: Unconsecrated
chapters.summary: Kestrel digs where the ledger points and finds the small coffin under the kitchen floor, along with the melted bell's clapper, buried beside it as a weight. The house goes utterly still around them. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: terrible clarity — belief arrived not as faith but as evidence in their hands.

chapters.title: The Bell Answers
chapters.summary: Carrying the coffin toward the churchyard, Kestrel is followed by the whole village walking in silence, and the melted bell rings overhead from empty air, guiding them. The three descendants confess aloud what their parents did. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: communal reckoning — justice outside any court, witnessed by everyone.

chapters.title: Return
chapters.summary: They bury the child beside her mother's grave and hang the clapper in the empty tower. The house releases its held memories in a single flood; Kestrel drowns briefly in strangers' lives before surfacing. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: catharsis and cost — some of what floods in does not leave.

chapters.title: Survey Complete
chapters.summary: Hollowmere Farm stands empty and ordinary, appraised and sold. Kestrel files the report but keeps one page: a room measured in 1974 that matches no floor plan, only a memory now lodged permanently in their mind. POV: Kestrel. Emotional beat: quiet, unresolved aftermath — the house let them go, but kept a copy.
